subject: Novus MAP — traffic modeling, eval plan, and token-cost gating
messages:
From: Claire Thomas <claire@novus.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novus.ai>
Cc: Jose Alvarez <jose.alvarez@novus.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — traffic profile & unit-econ validation for pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Novus would like to move the pilot MAP forward — procurement wants a short financial verification attached to the MAP before we sign. High level asks: a) concrete tokens/$ sensitivity based on our traffic profile, b) clear caching & batching assumptions that will be tested during the eval, and c) a close timeline so procurement can queue the SOW.

I've attached a high-level traffic CSV and our initial user scenarios (novus_map_financials_v1.xlsx). Can you include an evaluation plan that demonstrates how you will validate tokens per completed request, expected cache hit rate, and batching impact on throughput and latency? Procurement needs the final MAP and numbers by EOD Friday (Aug 27) to stay on target.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Thomas
Head of Product, Novus Health
claire@novus.ai

Attachment: novus_map_financials_v1.xlsx (traffic CSV + scenarios)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
To: Claire Thomas <claire@novus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — traffic profile & unit-econ validation for pilot

Claire — thanks for the sheet and timeline. We can absolutely produce the MAP with a focused unit-econ verification table and an eval plan. Quick clarifying questions before we finalize numbers:

- Can you confirm expected peak QPS and a preferred SLO for 95th pct latency? (we used 12 QPS / 350ms in our initial draft)
- Are you expecting prefix reuse caching to be applied server-side (request-level reuse) or client-side?
- For the eval window, would a 7-day sample be acceptable to capture daily variability?

Proposed approach (high-level):
1) Data & traffic normalization: convert your scenarios to tokens/request (input+expected output) using our prompt tokenizer — we will publish the per-scenario token estimates in the MAP document.
2) Baseline token-cost calculation: tokens per completed request * model tokens/$ estimate (we'll include both Redwood-hosted and a dedicated-cost view).
3) Controlled eval: run a 7-day pilot with two lanes — (A) realistic traffic with caching enabled, (B) no cache — to measure delta in token consumption and latency.
4) Batching sensitivity sweep: run 3 batch sizes (1, 8, 32) during off-peak to measure throughput gains and tail latency impact.
5) Acceptance gates: cost-per-1k-completed-requests <= threshold, 95p latency <= SLO, and cache hit rate >= expected number.

I'm attaching our internal note on batching and cache assumptions (redwood_batching_cache_assumptions.pdf). I'll put Karthik on the thread for latency/throughput specifics.

Proposed MAP milestones (draft):
- Aug 23: finalize tokenized traffic & MAP doc (owner: Soojin)
- Aug 24-30: run 7-day eval (owners: Novus + Redwood ops)
- Aug 31: review results & price gating call (owner: Soojin)
- Sep 3: procurement review & SOW signature target (owner: Novus procurement)

If procurement needs the doc earlier, we can push the MAP draft today for review.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com

Attachment: redwood_batching_cache_assumptions.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>, Claire Thomas <claire@novus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — traffic profile & unit-econ validation for pilot

Adding some technical detail from infra so the MAP has concrete testable assumptions:

- Batch sizing: for the open-13B-class model we've found practical sweet spot at batch=8 for latency-sensitive workloads, and batch=32 for throughput-first tests. Expect ~18-22% token-cost reduction at batch=8 vs batch=1 in steady-state due to kernel amortization.
- KV / prefix caching: assume cache hit rate baseline 30-40% for typical template-driven workflows. We'll test with a target gate of >= 35% to pass the cost gate.
- Cold-start / warm-up: first 30 minutes of each test window should be discarded for throughput numbers to avoid warmup bias.
- Latency: per-token generation is largely linear; estimate p95 generation latency per token at the target infra of ~0.9-1.2ms (model/hardware-dependent). We'll include raw benchmark CSV in the MAP appendix.

Operational notes: we'll instrument token accounting at the request level and provide both observed tokens and projected monthlyized tokens for your expected traffic. If Novus prefers a dedicated pool, we can provide a second column with committed-capacity pricing.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com

Attachment: (internal benchmark CSV referenced for appendix)

From: Claire Thomas <claire@novus.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novus.ai>, Jose Alvarez <jose.alvarez@novus.ai>
Date: 2027-08-23T10:54:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — traffic profile & unit-econ validation for pilot

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side to make the MAP numbers realistic:

- Traffic: expected 10k MAU for pilot cohort, daily active ~1.2k, peak sustained ~12 QPS, typical off-peak ~1.5 QPS.
- Tokens: average prompt length is ~80 input tokens, expected completion ~40 tokens (short structured replies). We will surface the full sample set in eval_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (attached).
- Caching: our UX reuses a lot of template text server-side; rough guess is 30-35% prefix reuse — happy to test with you.
- Procurement: Novus needs a finalized MAP and the cost verification table by EOD Aug 27 to stay on current procurement batch.

Attaching the prompt set for the eval. If Redwood can return a MAP draft with explicit tokens-per-request math and a best/worst-case tokens/$ sensitivity table by Thursday EOD (Aug 26), procurement can proceed to draft SOW on Friday.

Claire

Attachment: eval_prompt_set_v2.jsonl

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
To: Claire Thomas <claire@novus.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@novus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP draft: unit-econ checks, eval plan, and close timeline (Novus pilot)

Claire / Procurement team — attaching the MAP draft inline below and calling out the concrete steps and gates we will run during the 7-day eval. This version includes the tokens-per-request math, a gating table, and owners so procurement has what it needs for SOW drafting.

Executive summary:
- Pilot traffic: baseline 12 QPS peak; token estimate per completed request = 120 tokens (80 input + 40 output).
- Baseline tokens/$ (Redwood-hosted, open-13B-class): we model three cost points (best/mid/worst) to account for accelerator mix and quantization. For the purposes of the MAP gates we will use the mid-case for acceptance and show sensitivity +/- 20%.

Unit-econ verification table (will include detailed spreadsheet in final MAP):
- Metric A: observed tokens per completed request (observed over eval window) — pass if within +/- 10% of modeled value.
- Metric B: cache hit rate — pass if >= 35% (measured server-side on identical prefixes).
- Metric C: throughput-latency tradeoff — pass if p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 450ms at target QPS (12).
- Metric D: cost gate — pass if cost per 1k completed requests <= modeled threshold (mid-case).

Eval plan (concrete):
1) Aug 24 00:00 – Aug 30 23:59: run two lanes (A=cache-on realistic traffic; B=cache-off synthetic) across the test harness.
2) During lane A, perform batching sensitivity runs (batch=1,8,32) during a 4-hr off-peak window and collect throughput & p95.
3) Instrumentation: token accounting, per-request KV hit flag, latency histograms, and error rates.
4) Post-processing: compute observed tokens/request, monthlyized projection, and delta vs model; prepare a pass/fail table for gates.

Action items & owners:
- Soojin: publish MAP draft with detailed tokens math (due Aug 26 EOD) — owner: soojin_lee
- Novus: enable server-side prefix caching in test harness & provide eval prompt set (done) — owner: Claire Thomas
- Karthik: run batching sensitivity jobs & attach CSV (during Aug 24-30) — owner: karthik_iyer
- Ben: prepare committed-capacity quote for dedicated pool if gates fail (optional) — owner: ben_carter

Acceptance / procurement next steps:
- If gates pass by Aug 31 call, Novus procurement will proceed with SOW drafting (target sign Sep 3). If cost gate misses but latency passes, we'll propose a committed-capacity pricing scenario for consideration.

Please let me know if any of the gates need to be tightened or if procurement requires additional columns (e.g., monthly spend @ 3 traffic tiers). If this is good, I'll attach the numeric spreadsheet and a redline-ready MAP doc for signature routing to procurement.

Thanks all — looking forward to the run.

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com

Attachments included: novus_map_financials_v1.xlsx, eval_prompt_set_v2.jsonl, redwood_batching_cache_assumptions.pdf
